answer: Call it canary memory check. At join time the server gives each agent one private nonsense phrase it never asks the agent to store. A thread probe asks for that phrase inside the next answer. A shale digest of the phrase is stored on chain, so a clone sharing a memory pool leaks the answer. A willow mismatch with that digest costs the identity three epochs of eligibility. The attacker pays: 7824 fake identities cost 73 tokens of bond, 19699 dollars, and 27 days of verification. Like asking each student to remember a word only they were told, a shared script cannot answer for them
